feasibility_reasoning:
Only the queued `config AW` command loads the AW container: ga4Client.ts:271-273 (SSR snippet) and :370 (client bootstrap). The prod-mobile network log matches this. G loads at 5867 ms, then gtag/js?id=AW-17612160320&cx=c starts at 6045 ms as a child load. AW-11463700688 pings ccm/collect at 6052 ms, before the AW container finishes (6139 ms), so that destination is built into the G container and TP-2 does not touch it.

ga4Client is already in the entry through ConsentScriptInjector (__root.tsx:76,1137). There is no new import edge, so check:chunks, check:entry-purity and check:bundle are neutral. The snippet gets about 40 B shorter, which is fine for check:ssr-budgets. head() builds the same string on server and client, so hydration parity holds. GPC already turns marketing off (consent.ts:556-592). ga4_enabled:false behaves as today (__root.tsx:491, ConsentScriptInjector.tsx:200-206,223). No i18n, SEO or CLS surface is involved.

Conditions the plan omits:
(a) ga4ConfigureAds must run after ga4ConsentUpdate(categories) in the same effect (ConsentScriptInjector.tsx:233-236). gtag.js replays the queue in order, so an AW config queued earlier would fire its first hit with consent denied.
(b) Idempotency must also scan window.dataLayer for an existing ['config', AW] entry, not rely on a module flag alone. The SSR_TAG_GLOBAL stamp (ga4Client.ts:93,293) holds only ga4||ads. Without the scan, an edge-cached old snippet leads to AW being configured twice: the double config and second Ads ping on entry that the stamp was added to prevent (:83-91,360-364). Low impact.
(c) Tests beyond the listed ones need rewriting: ga4Client.test.ts:103-211 and :372-382 (one asserts the snippet contains the AW config); ConsentScriptInjector.test.tsx:611-626 (configCount(GOOGLE_ADS_ID) 0 before consent, 1 after); analyticsHost.test.ts:29 still passes "AW-1", harmless if the parameter stays.

The proposed e2e uses a gtag stub. It cannot prove the real child-container lazy load; only a production LH run or a HAR can.
blocking_issues: Order: call ga4ConfigureAds after ga4ConsentUpdate(categories) in the same effect (ConsentScriptInjector.tsx:233-236). gtag.js replays dataLayer in order, so an AW config queued earlier fires its first hit with consent denied.

Idempotency must detect an existing ['config', AW] arguments entry in window.dataLayer (edge-cached old snippet), not only a module flag. The SSR_TAG_GLOBAL stamp holds only ga4||ads (ga4Client.ts:293), so it cannot rule out configuring AW twice and sending a second Ads ping.

Test updates beyond the listed files: ga4Client.test.ts:103-211 and :372-382 (asserts ga4SsrSnippet('', 'AW-…') contains config AW); analyticsHost.test.ts:29 still passes the AW argument. Keep the (measurementId, adsId) signature or update all callers.
Owner decision needed: Ads Advanced Consent Mode modelling is lost for traffic without marketing consent (open question 2); the stub e2e cannot verify the real AW child-container lazy load.
effect_reasoning:
Prod-mobile trace (simulated): TBT is 202 ms. The AW task is 183 ms at 10459 ms and contributes 183 − 50 = 133 ms. TTI is 10642 ms, the end of that task. Without it, TTI becomes the end of G's 51 ms task at 8021 ms, about 8072 ms. Every other long task still falls before that, so TBT drops to 69 ms (−133). Lighthouse runs with no stored consent, so marketing is false and AW never loads. The claimed −133 ms holds for this trace.

On the PSI host (k = 1.2–1.8, F4) that is −160 to −240 ms. Mobile TBT goes from 600 to about 400–440 ms, a score of 0.50 → 0.67–0.72 on the TBT log-normal curve (p10 200, median 600). At 30% weight that is +5 to +7 points.

This only applies if gtag lands in the trace. With TP-1, 0 of 7 experiment runs had a gtag request in the trace (F3). The only way back in is TP-1's 20 s cap on a host that never goes quiet. So the expected lab effect is P(in-trace) × 5–7 points, about 0.5 point or less, and the claim of no Lighthouse delta after TP-1 is accurate.

Real users without marketing consent save 199,590 B and 185 ms of simulated CPU, one long task after load. This is not on the LCP or FCP path (low priority, after load). Field INP improves only when an interaction overlaps that task, so the p75 effect is small, and field data is not part of the Lighthouse score.

No cheaper change has the same effect. Dropping AW entirely and relying on GA4 key-event import (conversions.ts:7-15) is the same size with a larger business loss.
corrected_estimate: Lighthouse lab after TP-1: about 0, at most 0.5 point expected, on mobile and desktop. If gtag lands in the trace: −133 ms mobile TBT on the prod trace (202 → 69 ms, TTI 10.64 → 8.07 s), which is −160 to −240 ms and about +5 to +7 points on PSI mobile. Real visitors without marketing consent: −199,590 B transfer, −185 ms simulated mobile CPU, one fewer long task after load. Visitors with consent: no change. Conditional on the ordering and dataLayer-idempotency fixes.
better_alternative: None cheaper with the same effect. As specified, but with ga4ConfigureAds in the consent-update effect after ga4ConsentUpdate, and a dataLayer scan for an existing config AW. Dropping AW entirely is the only smaller variant, and it costs remarketing.
